newsitem.title: USA: Appeal set for Mo. school desegregation settlement.
newsitem.headline: Appeal set for Mo. school desegregation settlement.

text.p: Plaintiffs in a Kansas City, Mo., school desegregation case plan to file an appeal as early as Wednesday afternoon challenging a recent U.S. District Court approval of a monetary settlement between the school district and the state, an attorney for the plaintiffs said Wednesday.
Arthur Benson said he requested a stay of Judge Russell Clark's ruling on Monday, pending the imminent appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals in St. Louis.

Clark last month approved an agreement that would release Missouri from making court-ordered desegregation payments to the Kansas City School District. Under the terms of the settlement, the state would make final payments to the district of $105 million for the 1997-98 school year and $99 million for the 1998-99 school year.
The federal judge ruled that the state's 10-year, $1.3 billion payment to the district fulfilled all of its obligations under a 1986 court order.

However, Benson said the plaintiffs in the case, a class of 37,000 school children, will challenge that ruling on the grounds there is no constitutional basis to release the state from its obligation before the district has been declared to have met its desegregation goals.
"If the agreement is approved, it would require a substantial reduction in desegregation programs before desegregation goals are achieved," Benson said.
